action_history.rationale: Step 0 of a 10-experiment campaign (100% budget remaining) with only 5 initial data points in a 1D space. The data is sparse and we are in the early 'cold start' phase. Using max_variance to strategically place the next point where model uncertainty is highest, efficiently mapping the 1D landscape before switching to log_ei for exploitation. Matern-2.5 is the standard default for physical processes, and min_noise_low lets the GP learn the noise level freely from the clean-looking data.

Step 2 of 10 (90% budget remaining). We have 6 points in a 1D space with boundary coverage now established (x≈0 to x≈10). The highest y (0.74) is at x=10, suggesting the optimum may be near the upper boundary or in the undersampled x≈4-10 region. Switching from max_variance to log_ei to begin balanced optimization — log_ei will naturally probe the gap between x≈4 and x≈10 where both uncertainty and predicted improvement are high. Matern-2.5 and min_noise_low remain appropriate defaults for this smooth-looking 1D landscape with clean data.

Step 2 of 10 (80% budget remaining). The best y jumped from 0.74 to 0.966 — log_ei is clearly working and there is no plateau. With 7 points in 1D, the landscape is becoming well-mapped but likely still has undersampled regions between x≈3-10. Continuing with log_ei to maintain balanced exploration-exploitation, which will naturally probe promising gaps while refining near the current best. Matern-2.5 and min_noise_low remain appropriate for this clean, moderately smooth 1D landscape.

Step 3 of 10 (70% budget remaining). log_ei has driven two consecutive improvements: 0.74 → 0.966 → 0.9999, with the current best extremely close to what appears to be a natural ceiling of 1.0. The optimizer is clearly not stuck — it's converging rapidly. Continuing with log_ei to let it either confirm we've found the optimum by exploring remaining gaps (x≈3-10 is still undersampled) or refine the current peak further. Matern-2.5 and min_noise_low remain appropriate for this clean, smooth 1D landscape. No configuration changes needed when the current strategy is performing excellently.

Step 4 of 10 (60% budget remaining). The optimizer has performed excellently: best y improved from 0.74 → 0.966 → 0.9999 over consecutive steps, approaching what appears to be a natural ceiling of 1.0. The current best (0.9999) is near-optimal. With 9 data points in 1D, the landscape is reasonably well-mapped in the x≈0-4 region but the x≈4-10 region remains undersampled (only x=10 has been observed there). Continuing with log_ei because: (1) the strategy is clearly working with rapid convergence, (2) log_ei will naturally balance between refining the current peak and exploring the undersampled x≈4-10 gap where a secondary peak could exist, (3) no plateau has occurred so no escalation is warranted. Matern-2.5 and min_noise_low remain appropriate for this clean, smooth 1D landscape with good model diagnostics.

Step 5 of 10 (50% budget remaining). Best y=0.9999 is near the apparent ceiling of 1.0, achieved through rapid convergence (0.74→0.966→0.9999). The plateau is only ~2 steps old and the value is near-optimal, so escalation is unwarranted. The x≈4-10 region remains undersampled (only x=10 observed), and log_ei will naturally probe this gap if any predicted improvement exists there. log_ei remains the ideal balanced strategy at 50% budget with a well-calibrated model. Matern-2.5 and min_noise_low continue to produce good diagnostics on this clean, smooth 1D landscape.

Best y=0.9999 near x≈2, plateau is only ~3 steps (below escalation threshold), and the value is near the apparent ceiling of 1.0. However, x≈3-10 (70% of the domain) remains severely undersampled with only 1 observation at x=10. log_ei will naturally probe this gap if predicted improvement exists — it balances refining the current peak with exploring the undersampled region. With 4 experiments remaining (40% budget), log_ei is the ideal balanced strategy per budget guidance. Model diagnostics are consistently passing with matern_2.5 and min_noise_low on this clean 1D landscape.

Budget = 3 — strongly favor exploitation per budget rules. Best y = 0.9999 near x≈2, approaching a natural ceiling of 1.0. The plateau escalation protocol explicitly does not apply at budget ≤ 3. log_ei is the preferred safe choice: it will focus on refining the current peak region while still probing the undersampled x≈3-10 gap if the model predicts any improvement there. All diagnostics consistently pass with the current matern_2.5/min_noise_low/single_task configuration — no changes warranted. With 12 points in a 1D landscape, the GP should have a reliable estimate of where improvement is most likely.

Budget = 2 — strongly favor exploitation per budget rules. Best y = 0.9999 (effectively 1.0) near x≈2, which appears to be at or extremely near the global optimum of this 1D landscape. The plateau escalation protocol does NOT apply at budget ≤ 3. log_ei is the preferred safe choice per budget guidance: with 13 data points in 1D, the GP has a well-calibrated model (all diagnostics passing consistently), and log_ei will naturally focus on the narrow region around the current peak where any remaining improvement from 0.9999 → 1.0 might exist. The x≈3-10 region remains undersampled but log_ei will only direct a point there if the model predicts meaningful improvement, which is appropriate exploitation behavior. Matern-2.5 and min_noise_low have produced consistently good diagnostics throughout the campaign — no configuration changes warranted for these final experiments.

FINAL experiment (budget=1). Best y=0.9999 near x≈2, effectively at the global optimum ceiling of 1.0. Per budget decision rule #1, using UCB with very low beta=0.1 for maximum exploitation. With 14 data points densely sampled around x≈2 in this 1D landscape, the GP has a highly confident model of the peak region. UCB at beta=0.1 will place the final point almost exactly at the predicted maximum, squeezing out any remaining fractional improvement from 0.9999→1.0. The model has been consistently well-calibrated throughout (all diagnostics passing), so trusting its posterior mean for this final greedy step is well-justified. Matern-2.5 and min_noise_low remain appropriate — no reason to change a configuration that has worked reliably for 9 consecutive steps.
